sourceType: Official Government of Punjab tourism website
note: Facts (timings, entry fees, distances, locations) extracted below; prose summaries are written in our own words, not copied verbatim from the source. This site is organized by district (22 districts, each with its own page under /en/our-destination/<district-slug>/), unlike Puducherry's flat places-to-visit list. Only Amritsar has been scraped in full so far; other 21 districts remain for future sessions.

places.name: Sri Harmandir Sahib (The Golden Temple)
places.timings: Open throughout the day and night
places.facts: Blend of Hindu/Islamic architecture; construction started late 16th century by Guru Arjan Dev Ji; Maharaja Ranjit Singh renovated with marble/copper in 1809, gold-plated sanctum in 1830; four entrances symbolizing openness to all; Sarovar (holy tank) surrounds it.

places.name: Sri Akal Takht Sahib
places.facts: First/primary seat of Sikh temporal & spiritual authority; established 1609 AD by Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji; built taller than Mughal-permitted height as an act of defiance; Miri and Piri flags stand in front; houses historic Sikh weapons.

places.name: Interpretation Centre (Golden Temple Complex)
places.facts: Underground multimedia museum, 4 galleries with 15-min videos on Sikh history; free English headsets.

places.name: Central Sikh Museum
places.facts: Paintings, artefacts, manuscripts on Sikh history/Gurus/warriors.

places.name: Sikh Museum
places.facts: Listed as a key cultural/heritage destination; limited detail given by source.

places.name: Gurudwara Baba Atal Sahib
places.facts: 9-storey tower memorializing Atal Rai (son of Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji, died age 9); each storey = 1 year of his life; terrace has panoramic city/temple view.

places.name: Town Hall Partition Museum
places.facts: World's first museum devoted entirely to the 1947 Partition; 14 galleries; photographs, personal belongings, Gallery of Hope for visitor messages.

places.name: Jallianwala Bagh
places.facts: Site of the 13 April 1919 massacre under Gen. Dyer's orders during a peaceful Baisakhi Day protest against the Rowlatt Act; bullet-marked walls and the well where people jumped to escape gunfire are preserved.

places.name: Heritage Street
places.timings: Accessible at all hours; best in the evening
places.location: Town Hall to Sri Harmandir Sahib, Amritsar
places.facts: ~1km pedestrian stretch, Mughal/Rajputana/Sikh-inspired architecture with pink-toned facades; live Gurbani Kirtan LED screen; statues of Maharaja Ranjit Singh, Dr B.R. Ambedkar, Parliament House replica, Jallianwala Bagh memorial statue.

places.name: Gobindgarh Fort
places.entryFee: Rs. 180–649 Indians / Rs. 250–1000 foreigners (varies by attraction)
places.facts: Built 1760s by Gujjar Singh Bhangi, rebuilt by Maharaja Ranjit Singh early 1800s; was under Indian Army control until restored/opened to public; now a theme park with Tosha Khana coin museum, Haat Bazaar, Whispering Walls projection show (7:15pm Punjabi/7:45pm English), Sher-e-Punjab 7D film, Spirit of Punjab live show, Ambarsari Zaika restaurant.

places.name: Shahi Qila
places.facts: Listed among key heritage destinations; minimal detail given by source (appears associated with Attari Border area per site's attraction gallery).

places.name: Khalsa College
places.timings: Accessible from outside at all times
places.facts: Built 1892 by architect Bhai Ram Singh Ji; 300-acre campus; frequent Bollywood/Pollywood filming location (Veer-Zaara, Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi).

places.name: Sri Durgiana Temple
places.location: Near Lohgarh Gate, ~1.5km from Golden Temple
places.facts: Also called Laxmi Narayan Temple; dedicated to Hindu goddess; originally 16th century, rebuilt 1921 by Guru Harsai Mal Kapoor in Golden-Temple-style architecture.

places.name: Bhagwan Valmiki Tirath Sthal (Ram Tirath)
places.facts: Believed birthplace of Luv and Kush; site where Valmiki wrote the Ramayana; gold-plated Valmiki statue; ~2km parikrama; annual 4-day Ram Tirath Fair in November.

places.name: Ram Bagh Palace
places.timings: Check locally for current museum hours
places.facts: Maharaja Ranjit Singh's summer palace; named for Guru Ram Das Ji; 4 gateways (deoris) in Punjabi/Rajasthani style; now a museum with his artefacts, replica golden throne, replica Kohinoor diamond.

places.name: Panorama (Maharaja Ranjit Singh Museum)
places.facts: Visual documentation of Ranjit Singh's life; depicts 6 of his major battles.

places.name: Sadda Pind
places.facts: 12-acre living village museum of Punjabi culture; folk performances, handicrafts, cuisine; 20 guest rooms for overnight stays.

places.name: Punjab State War Heroes' Memorial and Museum
places.facts: 45m sword monument with 4 lion heads; memorabilia from Maharaja Ranjit Singh era through the 1999 Kargil War; 7D theatre on 1965/1971 wars.

places.name: Attari-Wagah Border (Retreat Ceremony)
places.facts: Daily flag-lowering ceremony with BSF Jawans and Pakistani Rangers; arrive 45 min early for seating.

places.name: Pul Kanjri (Pul Moran)
places.location: Near village Dhanoa Kalan, ~36km from Golden Temple
places.facts: Built by Maharaja Ranjit Singh as a trading post/resting place; complex includes a temple, Gurdwara, mosque and bathing tank; also has a 1971-war memorial.

places.name: Attari Samadhan Complex
places.facts: Samadhi of Sardar Sham Singh Attariwala, a general of Maharaja Ranjit Singh.

places.name: Sarai Amanat Khan
places.facts: Built 1640 by Amanat Khan, a Persian calligrapher who also inscribed the Taj Mahal; two gateways (Lahori Darwaza, Dilli Darwaza) lead to a courtyard with a mosque and well.

places.name: Amritsar Heritage Walk
places.facts: ~45-minute guided walk through old katras/havelis from Town Hall to the Galleria at Golden Temple.

places.name: Thatheras of Jandiala Guru
places.facts: Community of brass/copper/bell-metal craftsmen; UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage inscription 2014 (India's first).

places.name: Harike Wetland and Wildlife Sanctuary
places.timings: Daylight hours; early morning best for birdwatching
places.facts: Largest wetland in northern India, at the Beas-Sutlej confluence; Ramsar site; major bird sanctuary.

places.name: Hop-on Hop-off Tourist Bus
places.facts: City sightseeing bus service with tour guide — a service, not a standalone destination.

howToReach.air: Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport, Amritsar
howToReach.rail: Amritsar Central Railway Station — direct to Delhi, Chandigarh, Mumbai
howToReach.road: Amritsar Bus Stand — PRTC and private services
howToReach.local: Auto-rickshaws, cycle-rickshaws, Hop-on Hop-off Tourist Bus
